name: Clay
overview: Scripture reveals that man is intricately formed from the dust or clay of the ground, as God breathed life into him, making him a living soul (Genesis 2:7). This imagery is deepened by Job's reflections on humanity's fragile nature, dwelling in 'houses of clay' and fashioned carefully by God's hands (Job 4:19; 10:8; 33:6). Clay also serves as a symbol of transformation and divine craftsmanship, likened to the seal pressed into soft clay (Job 38:14) and representing deliverance from despair, as seen in the psalmist's rescue from the miry clay to firm footing (Psalms 40:2). Together, these verses highlight both the physical origin and the spiritual significance of clay as a metaphor for God's sovereign shaping of human life.
